author: massicomar
title: Elevator Rides
summary:
There are $n$ people who want to get to the top of a building which has only one elevator. You know the weight of each person and the maximum allowed weight in the elevator. What is the minimum number of elevator rides?

Input

The first input line has two integers $n$ and $x$: the number of people and the maximum allowed weight in the elevator.

The second line has $n$ integers $w_1,w_2,\dots,w_n$: the weight of each person.

Output

Print one integer: the minimum number of rides.

constraints.text: n ≤ 20 people, weights and capacity x ≤ 1e9

explanation: n ≤ 20 → bitmask. Weights are too large for knapsack. Store a pair per mask: (rides used, weight in the last ride), minimized lexicographically.
traps: Storing only the number of rides loses whether the next person fits in the current ride.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[mask] = lexicographically smallest (rides, load of the last ride) for carrying exactly the people in mask
dp[mask] = minimum number of rides for the people in mask
options.why: Not enough: two ways with equal rides differ in how full the last ride is.

options.text: dp[w] = minimum rides with total weight w
options.why: Weights up to 1e9; and it ignores who has been carried.

options.text: dp[i][mask] = rides when person i is the last one
options.why: Order within a ride doesn't matter; the extra dimension doesn't capture the load.

extraLayers.explanation: Fewest rides first, then the emptiest last ride — that pair is all the future needs.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: For each p ∉ mask: if load + w_p ≤ x → (rides, load + w_p), else (rides + 1, w_p); keep the min pair at mask ∪ {p}

options.why: Opens a new ride for every person.

options.text: Sort by weight and pack greedily (first fit decreasing)
dp[mask] = min over submasks s that fit in one ride of dp[mask \ s] + 1

extraLayers.explanation: Add one person at a time to the last ride, or start a new ride. O(n · 2^n).

es.explanation: n ≤ 20 → bitmask. Los pesos son demasiado grandes para una mochila. Guarda un par por máscara: (viajes usados, peso en el último viaje), minimizado lexicográficamente.
traps: Guardar solo la cantidad de viajes pierde si la próxima persona entra en el viaje actual.

dp-state.explanation: Primero la menor cantidad de viajes, después el último viaje más vacío: ese par es todo lo que el futuro necesita.

why.b: No alcanza: dos formas con los mismos viajes difieren en qué tan lleno está el último.
why.c: Pesos de hasta 1e9; además ignora a quién ya se llevó.
why.d: El orden dentro de un viaje no importa; la dimensión extra no captura la carga.

dp-transition.explanation: Agrega una persona por vez al último viaje, o empieza un viaje nuevo. O(n · 2^n).

why.b: Abre un viaje nuevo para cada persona.
why.c: El greedy de bin packing no es óptimo.
